record.paper_title: Cooperative Games with Incomplete Information: Some Open Problems
record.context_brief: Relaxing IPV and ex ante commitment assumptions
record.original_question: Can the core-based results obtained for Bayesian games with transferable utility under independent private values and ex ante coalition commitment be extended when one relaxes either the independent-private-values assumption, the ex ante coalition-commitment assumption, or both?

evidence.quote: Independent private values in the basic game G and ex ante commitment of coalitions play a crucial role in the previous results and relaxation of these assumptions is an obvious topic for future research.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a Bayesian cooperative game with transferable utility defined as follows. A finite set N of players is given. Each player i ∈ N has a finite type space T_i; let T = ∏_{i∈N} T_i. A prior probability distribution p on T is given, and the basic game G specifies, for each coalition S ⊆ N, each profile of actions, and each type profile, a transferable monetary payoff. Under the independent private values (IPV) assumption, p is a product distribution p = ∏_i p_i on T, and each player's von Neumann–Morgenstern utility depends only on actions and on his own type. Under the ex ante coalition-commitment assumption, coalitions form and commit to (incentive-compatible, state-contingent) cooperative agreements before players learn their types.

Under these two assumptions (IPV and ex ante commitment), a body of results characterizes various notions of the core (ex ante, interim, coarse, fine, etc.) for such Bayesian TU games, including non-emptiness theorems, balancedness conditions, and equivalence results.

Problem. Extend these core-based results to Bayesian TU games in which (a) the independent private values assumption is dropped, allowing correlated types and/or common-value components; (b) the ex ante coalition-commitment assumption is dropped, allowing coalitions to form at the interim stage (after players learn their types) rather than at the ex ante stage; or (c) both assumptions are simultaneously dropped. Specifically, formulate appropriate notions of the core in each of these relaxed settings and establish corresponding existence (non-emptiness), characterization, and equivalence theorems analogous to the IPV/ex-ante-commitment case.
artifact.category_tag: Bayesian cooperative games with incomplete information
artifact.status_search_result: The literature on Bayesian cooperative TU games (e.g., Forges–Minelli–Vohra, Myerson's virtual-utility core, Forges–Serrano surveys) treats relaxation of independent private values and of ex ante commitment as an active and largely unresolved research direction. Partial progress exists for specific solution concepts (e.g., interim core variants, virtual-utility cores, NTU extensions) but no comprehensive extension of the core-based results to non-IPV and/or non-ex-ante-commitment settings has been established. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Private information, transferable utility, and the core
status_evidence.snippet: Core analysis of Bayesian TU games under independent private values with ex ante coalitional commitment.
status_evidence.claim: Existing core results rely on IPV and ex ante commitment, leaving relaxations as open.

status_evidence.title: On the values of Bayesian cooperative games with sidepayments
status_evidence.snippet: Studies values for Bayesian TU games; incentive compatibility limits transferability when private values are relaxed.
status_evidence.claim: Relaxing IPV introduces obstacles not yet fully resolved for core-based analysis.

status_evidence.title: Virtual utility and the core for games with incomplete information
status_evidence.snippet: Myerson's virtual-utility approach to cores under incomplete information, including non-IPV settings.
status_evidence.claim: Some progress on non-IPV cores via virtual utility, but a full extension of the IPV/ex-ante results remains incomplete.
